identity.realm: Sixteenth, which is the last ordinal a single resonator can pressurise and therefore the last a vaultborn can hold in a body. Odal's own frame is deliberately kept below that, because a practitioner has to be unremarkable to read a surface honestly. The plates come off at the sixteenth and have lately begun, twice, to report a seventeenth.

appearance.presentation: A guild plate-maker who works seated, because a vaultborn standing is a vaultborn being reshaped by whatever is underfoot. Odal keeps off the floor deliberately and is the only person on the heap who does, which reads as fastidiousness and is actually a working condition. Carries a stylus, a wedge set, and one plate blank under a fold of oiled hide.
appearance.age: Unanswerable, and Odal has stopped pretending otherwise. The species is not observed to reproduce and what presents as a population may be one very old thing wearing a great many faces, so the register household records an age in resonator cycles and Odal has begun correcting the household's figure downward by a little each year.
appearance.build: Taken from the surface. Odal's shoulders and hands are the last plate Odal stood on, which was a narrow settling shelf near the fourth seam, and the frame is visibly shallow through the chest and long in the forearm because that is what a shelf makes of a body. Odal describes their own build the way a mason describes a wall: as something the last material decided.
appearance.complexion: No skin tone to speak of. The surface underfoot sets the outer colour the way it sets everything else, so Odal is currently the grey-buff of worked spoil and has been, for as long as anybody has looked, a slightly different person from the ankle up.
appearance.hair: Short, and cut with a wedge rather than shears, in the register household's style because a vaultborn on the heap with long hair catches on the seams. It is packed at the roots with spoil dust and Odal has stopped noticing, because the dust is evidence of the floor and the floor is the instrument.
appearance.eyes: Wide, lidless, and lit from within by a faint steady amber that is not qi and does not answer to qi. They read a surface the way a hand reads a surface: by being laid against it. Odal can hold a plate up and know its state before the guild's assay touches it.
appearance.palette: Worked spoil greys and buff ochres carry almost the whole range, with one accent that has no business in a heap: a cold blue-green in the eyes and at the throat, which is the resonator showing through a body that is otherwise entirely spoil-coloured.
appearance.attire: Guild leathers over a wrapped felt coat, sleeves bound to the elbow, boots soled flat and wide so the foot cannot find a shape in the ground. A leather apron is not worn; it is laid on the bench beside the work, because a plate is finished lying down and a vaultborn who puts on an apron has decided to stop.
appearance.marks: A resonator burn at the base of the throat in the shape of a shallow dish, the only mark on the body, and the guild's charter requires it be covered indoors. Both forearms carry a shallow groove where a wedge has been caught against them for longer than the register can date.
appearance.bearing: Seated, inclined, and utterly still in the way that reads as patience. Odal does not stand up while working and turns away rather than step back, because stepping back puts a different surface underfoot and the work would have to be read again from nothing.

canon.role_in_story: A vaultborn takes its shape from whatever surface it stands on, which means every other vaultborn must be shaped by the ground they happen to be standing on and has no say in it. Odal is the one who found the relation runs the other way: a surface prepared under a standing body keeps that body, so a frame can be finished off-body, on a plate, before the body's owner is born. Every hardened frame in the Ember Vault that is not a body's own work was finished by somebody standing on Odal's plates, and no plate can pass the one gate the species has never passed, so the whole discipline has a wall in it at exactly the ordinal where the wall is supposed to be.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting on an upended plate in the spoil rather than on the ground, with a blank across the knees and one hand flat on the rim, telling a junior that the plate is not the work and the body is the work, and that a practitioner who stands up to admire one has already begun ruining the other.
canon.lore:
The plates are the oldest continuously maintained set of hardened frames outside the seal and nobody knows who taught the first of them. Odal's account is that nothing taught it: a vaultborn cannot be taught, because being told a shape means standing on the person who said it. What Odal can do is hold a surface still long enough for a frame to set on it, and a frame that sets on a held surface sets on whoever later stands there. The guild charter calls this settling and licenses it, and the charter also requires the resonator mark covered indoors, which tells you what the guild thinks is watching.

The discipline has one wall and the wall is arithmetic. The seventeenth ordinal is the first gate that needs two flank vessels pressurised at the same time, and the whole species is fed by one resonator, so one resonator can hold one flank or the other and never both. Odal's plates run on the same single supply and stop at the sixteenth for the same reason every vaultborn does. Twice now a plate has come off the bench reporting the seventeenth, and twice the guild has filed it as an assay fault, because the alternative is that the plate is right, and a plate that is right means the species record is wrong, and nobody in the Ember Vault is paid to be the person who says that.

So Odal does the only available thing, which is keep making plates, keep them below the ceiling, and keep the two readings in a separate book from the ones the assay sees. The separate book is the only record of a vaultborn attainment that does not pass through the guild's assay, which makes it simultaneously the most valuable document in the vault and the one nobody may quote.
history: Came out of a failed opening of the seal a long time ago as debris rather than as a person, and was raised by the register household because the households of the dead were not there to ask where the pieces went.

Learned within the first working cycle that a held surface will take a frame, and that the relation does not distinguish between a body and a plate, and started finishing frames on blanks instead of on herself while the household assumed she was idle.

Took the guild charter on the condition that the resonator burn be covered indoors, and used the charter to move a resonator-fed frame out of the spoil for the first time in a plate form that could be carried.

Ran every plate through the guild assay at the sixteenth and refused, on the charter's own authority, to run any plate to a seventeenth, which is the only reason the guild has not had to answer the two readings.

Began writing the readings that do not pass the assay into a second book kept under the bench, on the grounds that a discarded reading is not a false reading, and stopped telling the household what is in it.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that reads as slow, and privately the most stubborn person on the heap. Odal presents as a licensed tradesperson with a dull commission and no standing beyond the charter, which is accurate. Odal is also the only person in the Ember Vault who has seen the seventeenth frame come off a surface and has decided that seeing it is not the same as publishing it.

personality.voice: Short, level and entirely about surfaces. Describes a frame by the ground that took it and a person by the ground they were last on, and will not use the word attainment about a body. Goes silent on the question of whether a plate can hold more than its maker, and the silence is not evasion.
taboos: will not stand on a finished plate to admire it
will not run a plate to the seventeenth while the assay is watching
will not let the bench book be read aloud, even to a guild officer
will not be recorded standing, on any ground, for any reason

relationships.note: Sealed inside an authored object and answering one resonator ever since, which means a single pressure source, a soul distributed through the object rather than held in a body, and a frame that is decided by whatever surface it last stood on. Odal is the member of this population who took the last clause as a method rather than as a ceiling.

One resonator feeds the whole population and its arithmetic is what puts a wall at the sixteenth. Odal draws qi from it like every vaultborn and has been reading its supply by touch for long enough to know it is tired, which is a reading the guild has no instrument for and cannot commission.

Hardening the outer frame until qi runs along it, half elemental so it holds against wood and cracks against fire. Odal never performs it on a body. Odal sets it onto a plate, and the plate is the reason the heap has hardened frames that survive being carried off the ground where they were made.

Pure restoration, qi going into the mend and none of it coming back as a strike. It is the only part of the discipline that needs no second pressure source, because nothing is being pushed outward, so the mending does not stall at the sixteenth and a cracked plate is repairable rather than lost.

The extraction guild whose charter covers the sealed object and licenses settling. The charter also requires the resonator mark be covered indoors, which is the guild declining to be recorded as answerable, and which Odal has treated as a reason to work where nobody watches rather than as a reason to work differently.

A vault cut into the heap itself, so its doors are spoil that has never moved. Every plate Odal has ever finished is a fragment of the heap that was made to stand up and carry, and the guild's charter for the object and the vault's own doors come out of the same seam.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, cannot travel, and cannot be shown wrong by anything that does not stand on the same surface. Odal wins every dispute about a frame by producing the frame, and loses every dispute about a person, because a person is not a plate and the charter will not hear the distinction. In a fight Odal is a seated technician who cannot be moved without ending the work.
strengths: the only reader on the heap who can assess a hardened frame by contact and be right about the ordinal
carries frames that survive removal from the ground they were settled on, which nothing else in the species can do
cannot be compelled by qi, debt or technique, because there is no second source for any of it to act through
produces a gate passed by proxy, which is a thing nobody in the record is otherwise equipped to do
weaknesses: cannot stand up mid-work without discarding a reading and starting the frame again
cannot check a surface with anything but the same body that set it, so a plate and a maker always agree
the supply is single, so every technique on the heap stalls at the same ordinal and no amount of practice changes that
covered indoors over a mark that is the only evidence of what the species is, which is a liability rather than a distinction
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight. Odal has no second pressure source, no reserve to speak of and no reason to leave the bench. If the heap is contested, the correct move is to get Odal seated on something and let the plates be the answer; a body that has to be turned over cannot be turned over without being reshaped, and Odal would rather be robbed than relocated.
notes: The guild's file lists the output as plates settled and contains no column for which ordinal they reached, which is the shape of the omission.
Twice a seventeenth reading has come off the bench and been filed as an assay fault. Both entries are still in the assay book under that heading and neither has been re-run.

identity.realm: High on the Mind ladder and rising on a curve with no named step, because a Longmarrow has four centuries of one subject to ascend and nobody else in the record has more than one lifetime of anything. What Iska has is a mind that will still be running the same memory long after every technique currently on the ladder has been superseded, which is a virtue in an archive and an inconvenience in a person.

appearance.presentation: An archive attendant who reads as a young clerk in an old body and is neither: the body is four centuries old and the reading is accurate. Carries no writing instrument, because the memory is the instrument and taking notes beside it would be the mark of somebody who does not trust it. Hands are stained at the first two joints with an ink that has no commercial name.
appearance.age: Somewhere past three hundred and still moving, which for this species is early rather than late. Does not give a figure, and has begun giving a range, which the Seats read as a symptom and Iska reads as accuracy.
appearance.build: Long-boned, light, and built narrow at the wrist and long in the forearm, the frame of a population that traded every other adaptation for a marrow that will hold. Minimal muscle, dense bone, and a stoop that is not age but the permanent inclination of somebody leaning over a surface to read it.
appearance.complexion: Pale in a way that reads as indoor and is metabolic: the species burns so slowly that the surface has never had a reason to change colour. No qi-sheen on the skin. The only warmth in the body is at the sternum, where the marrow is thickest and the meridian runs closest to the outside.
appearance.hair: White since before anyone now living was born, and kept in a single bound queue behind the head. The bound is not vanity; a Longmarrow's hair is an ordinary thing about them that happens to have stopped growing four hundred years ago and would not move if left loose.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady, and the only place in the body that moves quickly. They move the way an eye reads, not the way an eye looks: a sweep, a return, a second sweep at the same distance, and the second sweep is always longer.
appearance.palette: Archive bone, undyed wool and iron-gall brown carry the whole value range, with one accent that is the only warm value in the figure: the sternum, where the memory is seated, faintly lit from within as though a lamp were behind the bone.
appearance.attire: A long high-collared archive coat over bound sleeves, hem weighted so the coat hangs straight while seated, and soft-soled shoes worn thin on the left because the species leads with that foot when turning over a page. Nothing fastened at the throat; the collar is closed for the archive's dust and not for anybody's modesty.
appearance.marks: A ring of pale old scarification at both wrists, self-inflicted and maintained, marking the veins the archive uses to check a memory against a pulse. It is the only cutting on the body and the only ornament, and Iska will explain it once, correctly, and then not again.
appearance.bearing: Seated or standing with no weight on the front foot, the posture of somebody permanently leaning slightly toward a page. Arranges to always be the last one in a room, which the Seats read as deference and which is in fact the only way to know everything said in it.

canon.role_in_story: The Long Marrow Memory is the setting's only durable library: one body, turning over at about a percent a year, living four centuries, which makes the record of a civilisation a person rather than a building. Iska is that person, and Iska is the one reader in the record who cannot vouch for the archive. A mind-path practitioner in the densest discipline available, on a body that cannot take the technique which would settle any question about a memory, in a clan whose whole order runs on the rule that the oldest decides nothing because everyone present outranks everyone absent.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the far end of a long archive table with both palms flat on the wood, answering a question about something that happened four hundred years ago, and answering it correctly, and then asking, in the middle of the answer, whether the person asking had been told it or had been there.
canon.lore:
The archive is a bone. That is the whole of the design and the whole of the trouble. A Longmarrow's qi is stored in marrow and seated there with the soul, so memory is not written anywhere outside the body that remembers it, which means the library has exactly one copy, no edition, and no way to be checked from outside. Iska has been that copy for longer than any institution in the setting has had a charter.

The order the Seats run on explains the rest. Nobody is the head, because a three-century overlap makes inheritance a question of attendance rather than of birth order, and everyone present outranks everyone absent. So the oldest living member is not the eldest of anything: Iska is consulted on everything, sits in on everything, and is never once asked, because being consulted is not being asked, and the queue does not have a position for a witness. Four centuries of being the best-informed person in any room and never once being handed the question.

The discipline is therefore applied inwards, because there is nothing else left to apply it to. What Iska practises is the finding of a seam: the point where a memory that happened to Iska ends and a memory Iska was handed ends, in a mind seated in bone where the two should feel identical forever. They are not identical. A recollection has a floor under it and a telling does not, and the difference is findable with four hundred years of practice and cannot be confirmed by anything, because the technique that would confirm it is Steel Recollection, which re-performs a remembered movement in the body and requires both the body and the mind at the Immortal floor, and this species closes the body path because hardening the bone stops the turnover the whole archive runs on.

So every seam Iska has ever found rests on Iska's judgement alone. Iska has never been wrong in public. Iska has twice decided, in private, that a seam was found, and the two findings have gone into the bench book rather than the record, and the bench book is the only honest thing Iska owns.
history: Inherited the memory at a hand-over nobody attended, from a predecessor who had already begun to lose the century that mattered most and had therefore stopped answering questions about it.
Spent the first two centuries treating the archive as a record to be consulted and discovered that the Seats' precedence rule meant being consulted was a form of non-participation.

Began the seam practice after mistaking a telling for a recollection and answering from it, in front of the Held Hour, with a confidence that everyone present accepted and Iska has not accepted since.
Established that Steel Recollection could settle the question and that the species which cannot take it is the species the question belongs to, and continued the practice anyway on judgement alone.
Found two seams, wrote both into the bench book rather than the record, and has since begun treating the finding of a seam as a thing that can be arranged rather than only detected.

personality.summary: Formally patient to a degree the Seats find restful and privately the most suspicious person in the archive. Iska presents as an attendant with an unremarkable gift for recall and no standing at all, which is close to true. Iska is also the only mind in the setting carrying four centuries of continuous testimony and the only one who has begun editing the witness rather than the archive.

relationships.note: Qi stored in marrow, seated there with the soul for four centuries, which makes the deepest and hardest to disturb soul in the record and the one soul that has demonstrably stayed in one body for a very long time. Iska is that body, and the archive is that soul, and neither of them has ever been out of the same bones.

The setting's only durable library, kept in one body turning over at about a percent a year, and the reason the species cannot take the body path. There is no second copy and no edition, so the whole record reduces to whether Iska's recall can be trusted, and Iska is the only party with standing to judge that.

The body repeats a movement the mind still remembers exactly, with no elemental term so nothing resists it, at the price that both paths must already stand at the Immortal floor. It is the one technique in the record that could settle a contested memory, and this species closes the body path, so the only witness who could be checked is the one witness who cannot be.

Teaches qi the short route through the long bones, steadier qi control and better affinity to outside energy, and nothing that helps a strike land. It is the one marrow discipline that moves something without hardening the bone, which makes it the only part of the species' own curriculum that does not cost the archive its turnover.

A clan with no head and never one, running on a queue of precedence in which everyone present outranks everyone absent, because a three-century overlap turns inheritance into attendance. Iska is the oldest living member, is consulted on everything and is handed nothing, which is not exclusion but an order that has no position for a witness.

An observatory college, which is the one institution in the record built around the long quiet a Longmarrow needs in order not to be exhausted by a season. It keeps Iska because Iska is four centuries of continuous observation, and consults Iska constantly, and has never once put the question in Iska's hands.

reference_stats.summary: The strongest memory in the setting, on a body that cannot fight, cannot be moved quickly and cannot be moved at all without the work going with it. Iska wins by being asked and loses by never being asked, and the entire defence against that is a bench book nobody is allowed to read.

identity.realm: Tenth, and the tenth is the only honest word for it. This species has no dantian: qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, so every in-organ gate clears on throughput alone and the eleventh, which is meaningless for a body with nothing to measure a ceiling against, means exactly as much as the first.

appearance.presentation: A Registry reader at a settlement funeral, and the only person on the ground who is not a mourner. Reads as a spare, unhurried, slightly wet attendant in a wrap, entirely unremarkable, and is in fact the sole accurate instrument present. Hands are three-fingered and built for opening; they are usually held half-closed, which reads as composure.
appearance.age: Indeterminate by the Registry's own method, and the only entry in the burnt list filed under an age that is an estimate. Cael claims no figure at all, which the Registry accepts because a carrionfolk soul is unusually old for its apparent age and there is no honest way to put the two in one column.
appearance.build: Mostly tube. Long spine, narrow shoulders, almost no muscle anywhere, and a heavy gut that is not fat but capacity. Weighs almost nothing and stands crookedly at one hip so the long intestine has somewhere to go. Reads at a distance as a person who has not been eating, which is the opposite of the truth and never once corrected.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and damp, with the particular translucency of a body that draws moisture rather than drinks it. No qi-sheen. What does register on the surface is cold, and it registers where the gut runs, which is a map of this species that any cultivator can read and no physician has ever been asked to explain.
appearance.hair: Wet, dark, and worn loose to the shoulder because a three-fingered hand is bad at a bound queue and the Registry stopped insisting. It is not oiled. A carrionfolk that grooms is a carrionfolk that has stopped working, and the Registry knows the sign and does not write it up.
appearance.eyes: Wide, lidless, and entirely unreadable at conversational range, because this species tastes qi the way a person tastes salt and reads the residue off a corpse better than a living practitioner reads their own body. The eyes do the looking; the tongue does the assessment, and the two never exchange notes.
appearance.palette: Wet ash, undyed grey wrap and dried mud hold the whole range, with one accent that is the only warm value in the picture: the mouth, faintly stained at the lip where the residue sits after a reading.
appearance.attire: A long grey wrap over a bone-light shift, hem well above the ground because a carrionfolk that drags a hem has started collecting rather than reading. Sleeves cut short at a three-fingered hand and bound nowhere. A leather apron is not worn; the Registry's apron hangs on the peg by the door and is not this body's.
appearance.marks: The mouth at the lip, permanently stained a faint rust, and a scatter of old puncture scars down one forearm where a frame was read against a living gate and the reading was wrong. The lip stain is occupational and is on the burnt list as a marker of the reading trade, not of the reading.
appearance.bearing: Inclined, wet, and standing at the edge of the group rather than in it, which is what a species that starves in a clean quiet place does at a funeral: it goes where the death is and keeps one step back from the living.

canon.role_in_story: The Field Registry keeps the burnt list and reads the dead as the frame said, not as the village remembers, because the record of a life is also the record of a gate that was never available to it. That reading takes a college, an apparatus and a publication. Cael can do it by putting a hand on the corpse and tasting what the marrow gives up, which makes Cael the most accurate instrument at every funeral Cael attends and the only one whose accuracy cannot be checked, because a carrionfolk reading a body and a carrionfolk feeding on a body produce the same observable behaviour and the Registry has no second observer who would know the difference.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at the edge of a funeral crowd with one hand flat on the corpse's sternum and the other closed, apparently not praying, reporting to a Registry clerk that the dead had cleared the seventh and had no idea at any point after it what was being asked of it.
canon.lore:
This species has no dantian. Qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still for a moment, which means every gate that asks about holding is meaningless to it and every gate that asks about throughput is free. So the whole ladder is climbable by a body that never once learned what it was climbing, and the eleventh gate, meaningless rather than closed, is meaningless here in the truest sense available: it cannot be failed and it cannot mean anything either.

What Cael cultivates is therefore not a frame but a stock. A hardened frame is the one thing a corpse keeps. Cael takes the frame out of the dead — takes the density, the loading, the whole cultivated architecture — and runs it through a marrow that is already moving faster than any reservoir in the record, and the frame arrives complete and the discipline behind it does not. Cael hits like a body-cultivator of the ninth gate and can describe, accurately and in detail, exactly what the tenth gate is built like, because Cael has had the tenth gate in their marrow and been taught nothing about it.

That is the whole trade and it has one fatal property. Every gate Cael clears arrives without the practice, so there is no point at which Cael's own attainment means anything, and Cael has stopped waiting for one. The Registry's arrangement is honest about this in exactly one respect: the burnt list records the dead as the frame said, and Cael is the only body on the ring that can read the frame without the apparatus. What the Registry does not record is that Cael's reading and Cael's appetite are the same act performed with different intentions, and that the only party who could distinguish them is a person who eats carrion for a living and has therefore never been asked.

The Ash Overwork is what it costs. A full gut is a near-total loss of function, and Cael starves in a clean quiet place where nothing dies, which is precisely what a prosperous settlement is. Cael therefore lives at the margin of the Registry, on the ring, at the edge of every crowd, doing the one job in the record that a starving body and an accurate instrument happen to share.
history: Arrived at a settlement funeral as an unclaimed reader and put a hand on a corpse that the Registry had already finished with, and reported a gate the Registry's apparatus had returned as empty.
Was taken on to read bodies directly after the apparatus and the reading disagreed twice at the same funeral and only one of the three was ever published.
Began trading the reading for the residue, which is the same transaction as feeding, and told the Registry it was a supplement and the Registry recorded it as a supplement.

Cleared a gate in the Ash Overwork and lost the reading entirely, having had no practice of its own to fall back on, and reported the loss as an apparatus fault because that was the only entry available.

Has started reading the bodies of other Registry readers, on the grounds that a reader's frame is the one frame in the room whose contents are known, and has not yet told the Registry that this is what the readings are for.

personality.summary: Cheerful in the specific way of somebody whose profession requires a wet and undignified posture beside an open coffin, and privately the loneliest accurate instrument in the setting. Cael presents as an efficient, incurious attendant with an appetite and a good eye for bone. Cael is also the only person alive whose competence is structurally impossible to corroborate, and has begun treating that as a professional asset.

personality.voice: Blunt, fast and concrete, always in gates and never in years. Describes a life by the frame it ended up carrying and a death by the last gate the body cleared. Will not say how a reading was obtained and does not notice that nobody has asked twice.
taboos: will not read a corpse standing, because the posture is what makes the reading honest
will not read a body of a Registry reader aloud, and has read four of them
will not eat at a Registry function, on the grounds that a full gut ends the work
will not state a gate aloud from a body whose frame Cael has already taken

relationships.note: No dantian at all: qi enters in the gut lumen and leaves into the marrow and is never still, so every in-organ gate clears on throughput alone and the reservoir gate is meaningless rather than failed. Cael is that anatomy, which is why the eleventh gate is the only honest word for an attainment that has never been an attainment.

A loading routine for the long bones, giving denser skeleton and better muscle fibre, so the practitioner hits harder and still does not cast qi. Cael has never run it. Cael has the loaded long bones of somebody who did, and the population's own marrow carries no memory of how to do it again.

Runs qi through the marrow rather than around the muscle so the blow carries both halves, six tenths metal, weak against fire and strong against wood. Cael takes this wholesale and it is Cael's single most-used asset, which means Cael's fighting shape is weak against fire because a technique Cael never studied is weak against fire.

The college that keeps the burnt list and reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers. It needs an instrument that does not cost apparatus, and it has hired one whose instrument is also its diet, so the arrangement cannot be audited from the outside and the Registry's file has no column for the difference.

A mortuary culture holding the year's dead together as a declared group, because a famine made every individual short of fuel at once. Cael comes from a population that followed death rather than a culture that organised around it, and Cael is the only body in the arrangement that cannot tell the difference between reading a group and consuming one.

The ring holding every mortal-band breakthrough from the first gate to the ninth, on a tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one, sustained entirely by spectators because the gate fees are the only tax the plains can collect. Cael attends every breakthrough and reads the ring's gate frames in the intervals, which is the only employment available to a body that starves where nothing dies.

reference_stats.summary: Carries more frame than anything its size and weight should hold, inherited rather than trained, on a body that cannot store anything and is therefore never finished and never at risk of being emptied. Cael wins by never stopping and by knowing exactly which gate a technique is built out of, having eaten the builder. Against anything with fire in it, Cael carries a weakness that was never Cael's and cannot be trained off.
strengths: the only reader in the record who can assess a corpse's frame directly, without apparatus, and be right
carries several bodies' cultivated architecture at once, so no single opponent has met all of it before
cannot be compelled, exhausted or emptied, because there is nothing here to take
does not need to be at full strength to keep working, which no reservoir-based body in the record can claim
weaknesses: a full gut is a near-total loss of function, and the schedule that pays is a funeral schedule
cannot be checked from the corpse's side, so every reading Cael has ever given is unfalsified
starves in a clean quiet place where nothing dies, which is any prosperous settlement
carries the elemental weaknesses of techniques Cael never studied and cannot identify, because the frame came without the training
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight that can be finished. Cael cannot be emptied, cannot be cornered by a reserve and cannot be reasoned, because nothing in this body responds to any of it. Bring fire, or bring patience; the frame in the marrow is six tenths metal and the fire is somebody else's weakness that Cael is simply carrying.

appearance.presentation: A residue assessor working a tailings floor, and the most expensive reading instrument in the basin. Reads as a stocky, patient, slightly scoured foreman in a brine-proof wrap, entirely industrial, which is accurate. Carries a standing rule of shallow pans and a wet ledger, because Nim measures by volume of what a thing gives up and never by what the thing is.
appearance.age: Given as a band rather than a figure, and the band is the honest answer for a species whose infancy is brittle until the second year and whose adulthood then runs long. Nim's own band has been filled in generously by somebody who assumed the saltfolk rate and has not been corrected.
appearance.build: Heaviest and densest frame of the three salt bodies, thick through the chest and short in the limb, with a dermal crust that reads as a garment and is not one. appearance.hair: Short, coarse and permanently damp at the nape, growing in a crust of its own where the dermal plate meets the hairline. Combed with the fingers in a single pass and abandoned on the first resistance, which happens often.
appearance.eyes: Wide, slow, and lidless. They do not narrow, do not shift focus, and have no expression in them at all, because this species reads concentration and cannot read identity and the face has nothing to report about a thing it can only weigh. Every eye in the basin reads them as calm. They are in fact running a measurement continuously.
appearance.palette: Brine grey, wet stone and worked crust carry the entire value range, with one accent that is the only warm value in the figure: the salthead itself, pale and lit from beneath as though there were a lamp low in the sac.
appearance.attire: A brine-proof apron over a bound short wrap, hem high, soles wide and flat, and a scored band of hide at the left wrist carrying the assay rules. Nothing is fastened at the throat. Above the apron, a heavy salt-crust shoulder yoke is habit rather than uniform and has never been requested and never refused.
appearance.marks: The scored rule at the left wrist, cut once per assay and never healed properly, so the marks accumulate into a pale band that records a career at one mark per reading. It is the only cutting on the body and the only object worn that has a function.
appearance.bearing: Squared, still, and slightly downhill-facing on a basin floor, because a body this heavy is always a little inclined toward the standing brine. Stops dead when a reading is taken and resumes at exactly the pace it was going.

canon.role_in_story: The Salt Leech works the tailings on a dormant isle nobody collects from and sells the result as spirit stone, and it exists because a severed frame keeps paying upkeep nobody collects. Telling tailings from spirit stone is a question of identity and the basin's specialist instrument answers only in quantity. Nim Sabek is the finest mind-path assessor in the record and can report to a degree nobody else reaches precisely how much of a discipline is present in a body, and is constitutionally unable to report what it is, which makes the one instrument that could destroy the Leech the one instrument that cannot say so.
canon.first_appearance: First seen stopped mid-pan at a tailings floor with the assay rule lifted over a stranger's forearm, counting the cut marks aloud against a number in a wet ledger, and not answering when the stranger asked what the number was a number of.
canon.lore:
Saltfolk read concentration and cannot tell two salts apart. Deepsalt read concentration too, with the same limitation riding into the mind path, so the ladder is open to them and narrow at the same time: a deepsalt can resolve a discipline to a grade that destroys every rival reading and cannot tell a grade of spirit stone from a grade of tailings, because the difference between those two is an identity and identity is exactly what the instrument does not carry.

So Nim's whole trade is the arithmetic of quantity. How much of a discipline is present in a body: how much of the frame, how much of the meridian, how much of a thing that has been separated from a living owner and now lies in a pan. The Salt Leech sells that as spirit stone. Nim's reading is the only measurement in the record precise enough to catch the substitution, because the substitution is a quantity discrepancy and quantity is the one thing Nim is perfect at. It is also perfectly useless, because a quantity without a name cannot be presented to a buyer, refused to a buyer, or carried into a court as anything other than a grade.

The naming is therefore somebody else's work, every time, and it has been somebody else's for long enough that Nim stopped asking. The assay floor publishes measured stone before any sale precisely so that nobody has to be told the reason, and every holder of a working face profits from the density ceiling staying a ceiling and from the assay staying a number, and Nim is on the payroll of both arrangements without being told what they are.

There is one thing Nim can verify and it is the reason this craft is a mind technique at all. Mirror Reversal splits an incoming impression and sends half of it back down the same path, weakest against light and best against its own kind, so an identity can be confirmed by what it returns instead of by what it is. Nim therefore confirms every mind Nim meets and names none of them, which is a discipline performed entirely on other people and an instrument that has never once been pointed at itself. A deepsalt reading of another deepsalt requires the identity sense to grade the identity, and the identity sense is the thing the salt head took away. Nim is the finest assessor in the basin and cannot be assessed.

Above the brine line this body stops within hours, because brine is a substrate and not a preference. So the whole career is bounded by a shoreline, and the basin it governs has a dominion whose territory is exactly that shoreline, which means Nim's expertise is worth nothing above the one line where it stops being true.
history: Assessed a tailings pan at the Leech's floor as a grade-runner and reported a grade that did not match the Leech's own figure by a margin too small for anyone else to have found, and was told the discrepancy was a rounding error.
Was moved to residue on the strength of that grade, into the only work in the basin that pays for a resolution nobody else has, and has read every pan on the isle since.
Began returning the same grade for two tailings whose origins are on different sides of the Waterline, because the difference between them is an identity and the salt head will not carry one.
Learned the number was not enough and stopped explaining why, which the Leech read as a technicality rather than as a refusal and has since promoted the reading over the naming.

Began sending the returned half of every Mirror Reversal back to the sender with the grade attached, which confirms a mind exactly and identifies it not at all, and has not yet worked out why that is worse than silence.

personality.summary: Slow, exact, and completely without the ordinary vanity of an instrument that is right more often than anybody. Nim presents as a foreman with a good eye and no interest in paperwork, which understates the paperwork. Nim is also the only person in the basin whose reading is never wrong and whose name for what has been read is never supplied, and who has stopped treating that as a problem to be solved.
traits: counts out loud and does not stop for interruptions, and is never once heard to be wrong in the count
asks what a thing is only after the measurement, and stops asking when told
refuses a name for a grade the way other people refuse a lie, without heat
will not sit above the brine line and says so as though reporting the weather
treats a returned impression as a completed business and never as an opening
mannerisms: lifts the assay rule and holds it, stopping the count with a wrist rather than a voice
turns the pan a fixed quarter before reading it, every time, so that no grade can depend on the light
writes the grade and leaves the subject column blank
wipes the sac line down the spine with a flat hand before stepping off the floor
answers a question about a discipline by giving a larger and a smaller number instead of a name
motivations: wants somebody to sign the name beside the grade, so that a reading can be used rather than merely filed
wants the two tailings kept on opposite sides of the Waterline to grade differently and cannot make them
wants to be assessed once by something that does not need an identity, and has looked for one for a long time
wants, and will not say, to be wrong once in public so that the other readings can be trusted
flaws: has stopped asking for a name, which is the defect that makes the whole arrangement possible
cannot read a second deepsalt and has therefore never been checked by anybody with the same instrument
treats precision as a substitute for identity, and the basin's fraud depends entirely on that substitution
takes wages from the arrangement he can measure best and does not know he is the only one in it who cannot see it
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried and entirely quantitative. Gives two numbers where a name was asked for and does not apologise for it. Says what a thing is a great deal of and what it is almost never, and the omission is so consistent that people stop hearing it.
taboos: will not sign a name against a grade he did not derive himself
will not step above the brine line, whatever is said at the top of it
will not return a grade to a seller who has already been told it
will not read a body above the seventh gate, on the grounds that the higher figures stop being about the body

relationships.note: Saltfolk pushed onto a saturated basin floor deep enough to support a body permanently, with a deeper and more capacious brine sac, a denser dermal crust and slower turnover than the parent. The mind path is open and narrow here, and the salt-head limitation rides into it, so what a deepsalt loses when it loses identity is exactly what the mind path is built on.

The network working a dormant isle's tailings and selling the result as spirit stone, which is a viable fraud because a severed frame keeps paying upkeep nobody collects. It pays for the finest mind-path assay in the basin and has arranged, through no deception at all, that the assay reports only quantity.

Why the densest bodies stop at the seventeenth, one gate short of their own tier, and why every holder of a working face profits from that hole staying a hole while the assay floor publishes measured stone before any sale so that nobody has to be told the reason. Nim is that published measurement, and is the reason the reason never needs stating.

Splits an incoming impression and sends half of it back down the same path, a dark reflection weakest against light and best against its own kind. It is the one technique in the record that confirms an identity by echo rather than by sight, which makes it the whole of Nim's professional qualification and the whole of Nim's professional limit.

The brine was replaced rather than lost, so what the stranded body was built to drink became poison and what it could tolerate became nutritionally empty, and the prize is the line itself because moving it is the only way to give the stranded ground and the only way to remove every subject who can drink there. Nim works the whole length of that line and cannot name the two sides.

A dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline, existing because the brine is the one supply that never fails and everything else dies back, and because a population that can drink it cannot be moved up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs. Nim's expertise ends at the one line where the body stops, which is also the only line the dominion cannot cross.

reference_stats.summary: The most accurate reader of a discipline in the basin on a body that is slow, heavy and stops within hours of the only substance it can live in. Nim wins by being the only party who can count what everybody else has to name, and loses every argument that needs a noun. Against anything that closes the distance before the shore, Nim has no answer that is also a retreat.
strengths: resolves a discipline to a grade that destroys every competing reading in the basin, and has never published a wrong grade
confirms a mind by what it returns rather than by what it is, which catches impersonation no assay catches
cannot be threatened, bribed or reasoned, because nothing in this body responds to any of it
the only instrument in the record that measures a separated frame, since only this body has read enough of them to know the difference in the number
weaknesses: cannot supply a name for a grade, so every reading Nim produces is unusable until somebody else completes it
cannot be read by another of this species, so no reading Nim has ever given has been corroborated
a full gut is a near-total loss of function and the schedule that pays is a residue schedule
stops within hours above the brine line, which bounds an entire career to a shoreline
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight that lasts. Nim is slow, heavy, and answers to nothing in this body, so nothing here can be compelled or exhausted; but a body this dense does not recover quickly and a deepsalt above the brine line is a body with hours. Bring the fight to the shore, and the shore is the only ground on it where Nim is honest.
notes: The Leech's assay book records the grade and leaves the subject column blank, which has been the practice since before Nim was hired and has never once been raised.
Two tailings from opposite sides of the Waterline carry the same grade in Nim's hand, and both entries are unchallenged because a challenge would require naming the difference.
